status: private editorial material, not learner payload

questions.question: The sun rises approximately in which direction?
questions.answer: East; the rising point varies through the year.

questions.question: A learner faces south. What direction is behind them?
questions.answer: North.

questions.question: A map arrow points right. Where is north on that map?
questions.answer: Towards the right.

questions.question: On a north-up map, the clinic is left of the market. Give the direction from market to clinic.
questions.answer: West.

questions.question: A path shown on a map crosses a dangerous flooded area. What should you do?
questions.answer: Avoid it and ask a trusted adult for a safe alternative.

sections.teacherPrompt: Draw the same map twice, rotating the second drawing. Add north arrows to both. Trace the gate-to-library route and explain why its compass directions stay the same.
sections.assessment: Check the learner's explanation, accurate vocabulary and safe practical application; accept other correct responses. Offer a model and a fresh example when needed.

questions.question: Name one sub-county mentioned in Nakuru's plan.
questions.answer: Gilgil, Naivasha or Molo.

questions.question: Which has greater 2019 land area, Nakuru or Nyandarua?
questions.answer: Nakuru.

questions.question: Why should a map include its date?
questions.answer: Names, boundaries and information may change.

questions.question: Three full squares and two half-squares cover about how many squares?
questions.answer: Four.

questions.question: Explain why counting squares on maps of different scales is unfair.
questions.answer: The squares represent different real land areas.

sections.teacherPrompt: Use the KNBS reference-map source with an adult if available. Without internet, compare the two stated census areas and draw two equal-scale imaginary outlines of 12 and 20 squares. Explain why the outlines are examples, not real boundaries.
sections.assessment: Check the learner's explanation, accurate vocabulary and safe practical application; accept other correct responses. Offer a model and a fresh example when needed.

questions.question: What shape has a raised flat top?
questions.answer: A plateau.

questions.question: Can all valleys be assumed to contain rivers?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: Name a Kenyan lake mentioned in the lesson.
questions.answer: Lake Nakuru.

questions.question: Why can a steep slope be difficult for farming?
questions.answer: Soil can wash away and access is difficult.

questions.question: Why is clear river water not necessarily safe for drinking?
questions.answer: It may contain germs or pollutants.

sections.teacherPrompt: Sketch a profile with a high point, two slopes and a low valley. Add a stream in the valley. Label where water might collect and explain one way to prevent soil being washed away.
sections.assessment: Check the learner's explanation, accurate vocabulary and safe practical application; accept other correct responses. Offer a model and a fresh example when needed.

questions.question: How many rainy days appear in the example?
questions.answer: Three.

questions.question: Is a single hot afternoon proof that the hot season has begun?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: Why do pedestrians need extra care during rain?
questions.answer: Slippery surfaces, reduced visibility or flooding.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a weather-chart key?
questions.answer: It explains symbols or colours.

questions.question: Name two ways to prepare for a dry period.
questions.answer: Conserve water and plan farming appropriately.

sections.teacherPrompt: Draw five columns for weekdays and record the example observations using R for rain and S for sunny. Add a key. Compare the number of each type, then explain a safe activity for a rainy day.
sections.assessment: Check the learner's explanation, accurate vocabulary and safe practical application; accept other correct responses. Offer a model and a fresh example when needed.

questions.question: Name the museum near Nakuru discussed here.
questions.answer: Hyrax Hill Museum.

questions.question: What can a stone tool suggest?
questions.answer: An example of past work or technology.

questions.question: Why might a photograph be incomplete evidence?
questions.answer: It may not show the date or the reason for a change.

questions.question: How can a visitor protect a monument?
questions.answer: Follow rules, do not damage it or remove objects.

questions.question: What is the difference between a model and an original object?
questions.answer: A model represents it; the original is the actual historical object.

sections.teacherPrompt: Create a museum label for an imaginary old woven basket: object, possible use, what you know and what you still need to check. Keep real artefacts where they belong.
sections.assessment: Check the learner's explanation, accurate vocabulary and safe practical application; accept other correct responses. Offer a model and a fresh example when needed.

questions.question: What does a miller do?
questions.answer: Processes grain into flour.

questions.question: Give one unpaid example of interdependence.
questions.answer: Helping a neighbour or caring for someone.

questions.question: What could happen to a shop if the mill closes?
questions.answer: It may receive less flour.

questions.question: Why do producers need consumers?
questions.answer: Consumers use or buy their products.

questions.question: How can a group cooperate fairly when one member needs assistance?
questions.answer: Adapt tasks, include them and respect their contribution.

sections.teacherPrompt: Draw a household at the centre and link it to a farmer, shop, health centre and transport service. Add an arrow showing what the household gives or receives from each.
sections.assessment: Check the learner's explanation, accurate vocabulary and safe practical application; accept other correct responses. Offer a model and a fresh example when needed.

questions.question: Which had higher 2019 average density, Mombasa or Turkana?
questions.answer: Mombasa.

questions.question: Why can a large county have low density?
questions.answer: Its population may be spread over a very large area.

questions.question: What does a census count?
questions.answer: People, along with other information.

questions.question: Twenty people in one square kilometre give what density?
questions.answer: 20 people per square kilometre.

questions.question: Can a county average show the exact location of each home?
questions.answer: No.

sections.teacherPrompt: Compare the two 2019 county densities in the table. Make two equal boxes containing 20 and 5 dots, respectively. Explain the difference between the imaginary dot example and a real county average.
sections.assessment: Check the learner's explanation, accurate vocabulary and safe practical application; accept other correct responses. Offer a model and a fresh example when needed.

questions.question: Name two ways people express culture besides clothing.
questions.answer: Food, housing, artefacts, games or ceremonies.

questions.question: What is an artefact?
questions.answer: A human-made object.

questions.question: Why might a basket have a tightly woven base?
questions.answer: To hold small items more securely.

questions.question: Can every family in one community be expected to follow the same traditions?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: How should you respond to a classmate's unfamiliar tradition?
questions.answer: Listen respectfully, avoid stereotypes, ask only appropriate questions.

sections.teacherPrompt: Study a household object with permission or use a drawing. Make a three-part label: material, use, knowledge. Explain how it might be made differently today.
sections.assessment: Check the learner's explanation, accurate vocabulary and safe practical application; accept other correct responses. Offer a model and a fresh example when needed.

questions.question: Which event occurred earliest?
questions.answer: School opening in 2008.

questions.question: Which occurred last?
questions.answer: Library opening in 2021.

questions.question: What should a historian do if two records disagree?
questions.answer: Seek more evidence and note uncertainty.

questions.question: Give one example of a school value.
questions.answer: Honesty, respect, responsibility or similar.

questions.question: How could a rule reflect respect?
questions.answer: Listen when others speak, include peers or care for shared items.

sections.teacherPrompt: Make three event cards from the imaginary school evidence. Order them, then propose a motto and one fair rule that reflects respect.
sections.assessment: Check the learner's explanation, accurate vocabulary and safe practical application; accept other correct responses. Offer a model and a fresh example when needed.

questions.question: Name two natural resources.
questions.answer: Land, water, soil, forests or minerals.

questions.question: Is repairing a bicycle a good or a service?
questions.answer: A service.

questions.question: What output does the carpenter example describe?
questions.answer: A stool.

questions.question: Why should water users avoid waste?
questions.answer: Others and future needs depend on the resource.

questions.question: How could a trader reduce waste safely?
questions.answer: Reuse clean suitable packaging or reduce unnecessary packaging.

sections.teacherPrompt: Choose a familiar product or service. Draw four boxes: resource, work, output, benefit. Add a conservation idea. If working alone, use the stool example.
sections.assessment: Check the learner's explanation, accurate vocabulary and safe practical application; accept other correct responses. Offer a model and a fresh example when needed.

questions.question: Which industry produces flour from grain?
questions.answer: Milling.

questions.question: Give an example of a small-scale industry.
questions.answer: Tailoring or furniture workshop.

questions.question: Why might a dairy plant need reliable transport?
questions.answer: To receive milk and move products safely.

questions.question: What should workers do if packaging is damaged?
questions.answer: Check it and follow safe quality procedures.

questions.question: Name two possible benefits of industry.
questions.answer: Jobs, useful goods, income or value addition.

sections.teacherPrompt: Draw a grain-to-flour sequence with four stages. At each stage write one safe responsibility. Use a fictional location map with a road, farms and market to discuss possible industry locations.
sections.assessment: Check the learner's explanation, accurate vocabulary and safe practical application; accept other correct responses. Offer a model and a fresh example when needed.

questions.question: What is the total cost in the seedling example?
questions.answer: KSh 100.

questions.question: What is the surplus if receipts are KSh 130?
questions.answer: KSh 30.

questions.question: What is the loss if receipts are KSh 80?
questions.answer: KSh 20.

questions.question: Why should the group record both costs and receipts?
questions.answer: To understand the result honestly.

questions.question: Give two fair project rules.
questions.answer: Share tasks fairly; do not force contributions; adult supervision; accurate records.

sections.teacherPrompt: Make a paper plan for a bookmark or seedling project. Write a purpose, roles, safe materials, estimated costs and an imaginary sales total. Calculate the result. No real sale is required.
sections.assessment: Check the learner's explanation, accurate vocabulary and safe practical application; accept other correct responses. Offer a model and a fresh example when needed.

questions.question: Why is sharing pencils fairly good citizenship?
questions.answer: It includes everyone and respects shared needs.

questions.question: What is integrity?
questions.answer: Acting honestly even when no one is watching.

questions.question: Should a learner obey an unsafe request?
questions.answer: No; seek help from a trusted adult.

questions.question: What should you do before sharing another person's photo?
questions.answer: Ask appropriate permission.

questions.question: Give one way to include a learner who needs support.
questions.answer: Adapt the task, share materials or ask what support is helpful.

sections.teacherPrompt: Read the pencil-sharing example. Write two possible responses and explain which is fairer. Choose one realistic positive action and reflect on its effect without ranking classmates.
sections.assessment: Check the learner's explanation, accurate vocabulary and safe practical application; accept other correct responses. Offer a model and a fresh example when needed.

questions.question: Name two factors that promote peace.
questions.answer: Respect, fair rules, patience, listening or cooperation.

questions.question: Is silence always evidence of peace?
questions.answer: No; people may be afraid to speak.

questions.question: How could the reading-corner problem be solved?
questions.answer: Agree on fair turns.

questions.question: Should a child negotiate alone with someone threatening them?
questions.answer: No; seek adult help.

questions.question: How can a class check whether a peaceful plan works?
questions.answer: Review fair access and safe participation.

sections.teacherPrompt: Draw a two-column timetable for the fictional reading corner. Explain how both groups can have equal access. Write a safe response if someone threatens a learner.
sections.assessment: Check the learner's explanation, accurate vocabulary and safe practical application; accept other correct responses. Offer a model and a fresh example when needed.

questions.question: Do rights depend on good behaviour?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: Name two children's rights.
questions.answer: Education, care, dignity, safety or protection.

questions.question: Why is unsafe transport a child-protection concern?
questions.answer: It can place children at risk of harm.

questions.question: What should a child do if the first adult does not help?
questions.answer: Tell another safe adult and seek help.

questions.question: What is Kenya's national child helpline number?

sections.teacherPrompt: Create a fictional rights-awareness poster showing education, safety, care and inclusion. Add ways to get help. Do not include real names or personal stories.
sections.assessment: Check the learner's explanation, accurate vocabulary and safe practical application; accept other correct responses. Offer a model and a fresh example when needed.

questions.question: Which activity received more votes?
questions.answer: Story circle.

questions.question: How many learners voted in the example?
questions.answer: Twenty.

questions.question: Why is a secret ballot useful?
questions.answer: Protects the privacy of choice.

questions.question: Can a majority vote remove a child's rights?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: How could the class respect the eight learners?
questions.answer: Listen to them and consider an accessible future activity.

sections.teacherPrompt: Make a tally table for the imaginary 12 and 8 votes. Explain how the decision can respect everyone. Design a private ballot for two harmless fictional activities.
sections.assessment: Check the learner's explanation, accurate vocabulary and safe practical application; accept other correct responses. Offer a model and a fresh example when needed.

questions.question: Who records meeting decisions?
questions.answer: Secretary.

questions.question: What does a chairperson do?
questions.answer: Helps organise and guide discussion.

questions.question: How may a learner without a role participate?
questions.answer: Share suggestions or join safe approved activities.

questions.question: Who retains responsibility for school safety and discipline?
questions.answer: Responsible adults.

questions.question: What should minutes include?
questions.answer: Accurate agreed actions or decisions and relevant responsibilities.

sections.teacherPrompt: Write imaginary minutes for a council meeting about a reading corner. Include the topic, two suggestions, one agreed proposal and the adult who should review it.
sections.assessment: Check the learner's explanation, accurate vocabulary and safe practical application; accept other correct responses. Offer a model and a fresh example when needed.

questions.question: Name three kinds of leaders in the lesson.
questions.answer: Religious, clan and village leaders.

questions.question: Give a possible duty of a religious leader.
questions.answer: Spiritual guidance or community support.

questions.question: Why should a leader listen to different views?
questions.answer: To understand needs and make fair decisions.

questions.question: Who should handle hazardous waste in a clean-up?
questions.answer: Trained responsible adults.

questions.question: How can a leader demonstrate accountability?
questions.answer: Explain decisions, accept responsibility and review results.

sections.teacherPrompt: Plan a fictional community reading event. Assign safe roles, include learners with different needs and explain how the leader will check whether the event worked.
sections.assessment: Check the learner's explanation, accurate vocabulary and safe practical application; accept other correct responses. Offer a model and a fresh example when needed.

questions.question: How many county governments does Kenya have?
Who leads the county executive?
questions.answer: Governor.

questions.question: Which body considers county laws and oversees executive work?
questions.answer: County assembly.

questions.question: Does an MCA personally carry out every service?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: Give a safe way residents can raise a county service concern.
questions.answer: Use appropriate county feedback or representation channels.

sections.teacherPrompt: Draw two branches of county government. Put governor and executive committee under the executive; put ward representatives under the assembly. Explain the market example without inventing names of current officials.
sections.assessment: Check the learner's explanation, accurate vocabulary and safe practical application; accept other correct responses. Offer a model and a fresh example when needed.

questions.question: On a north-up map, a school is east of a market. Which direction is the market from the school?
questions.answer: West; reverse the direction.

questions.question: Explain why two county maps must have the same scale when comparing area.
questions.answer: Equal map distances must represent equal ground distances.

questions.question: Compare a plateau and a valley.
questions.answer: A plateau is raised fairly flat land; a valley lies between raised areas.

questions.question: A road is flooded and a friend wants to cross. What should you do?
questions.answer: Avoid crossing, seek a safe adult-approved alternative.

questions.question: Draw a chain from grain farmer to household and explain one connection.
questions.answer: Farmer → miller → trader → household; accept a correct relationship.

questions.question: Two equal squares contain 16 and 8 people. Compare their densities.
questions.answer: First has twice the density of the second.

questions.question: Explain a difference between population density and distribution.
questions.answer: Density is people per unit area; distribution is the pattern of where people live.

questions.question: Why may a scattered settlement need a different transport plan?
questions.answer: Homes are farther apart and may need accessible transport solutions.

questions.question: Choose an artefact and explain what it might tell us about a cultural practice.
questions.answer: Accept a specific accurate object, its materials, use or associated knowledge.

questions.question: Why should we avoid assuming everyone from one community dresses alike?
questions.answer: Families and individuals have diverse and changing traditions.

questions.question: Order these fictional dates: 2018, 2004, 2011.
Give one school value and a rule that reflects it.
questions.answer: E.g. respect: listen without interrupting.

questions.question: Identify a resource, economic activity and product in one example.
questions.answer: E.g. soil, farming, vegetables.

questions.question: Explain how an industry adds value to grain.
questions.answer: Milling changes grain into useful flour.

questions.question: A project spends KSh 150 and receives KSh 180. Calculate the surplus.
questions.answer: KSh 30.

questions.question: Name two ethical and safe practices for a school enterprise.
questions.answer: Accurate records, fair tasks, voluntary participation or adult supervision.

questions.question: What would a good citizen do with a lost item?
questions.answer: Return it through an appropriate trusted adult or safe process.

questions.question: Explain why a learner should not have to negotiate alone with someone threatening them.
questions.answer: Safety comes first; trusted adults must help protect the learner.

questions.question: What can a learner council do, and who remains responsible for safety?
questions.answer: Represent learners' views and propose activities; responsible adults retain safety duties.

questions.question: Distinguish the county executive from the county assembly.
questions.answer: Executive carries out county functions; assembly makes laws and oversees the executive.
